bull.b: Revenue is guided to grow 22%–25% in 2026 even before PAD, ENHANCE Part B or DENOVO contribute meaningfully. This indicates current OCS and NOP demand can support expansion independently, while the broader pipeline offers additional adoption avenues over the medium term.

Product and service revenue are both growing, while service reached 41% of total revenue and logistics grew 39% year over year. A larger case-based service mix can deepen customer integration and broaden recurring economics as transplant volumes and NOP coverage expand.

Cash of $473M plus restricted cash and positive adjusted operating income provide resources to fund OCS Kidney, Gen 3.0, and international expansion without relying solely on near-term revenue. This liquidity supports execution through planned investment while the platform scales.

bear.b: TTM operating and net margins have declined from 2025 levels, while management cut full-year adjusted operating-margin expectations to 12.5%–14% from 16%. Sustained investment and mix pressure could limit earnings conversion even as revenue continues to grow.

Debt-to-equity rose from about 1.0 in 2025 to about 1.6 in TTM, with total debt materially higher. Greater leverage reduces financial flexibility and adds sensitivity to profitability, especially while the company is funding several large strategic programs.

ENHANCE Part B and DENOVO contributed minimally, with approvals still pending and meaningful revenue timing uncertain; PAD integration and European reimbursement also carry execution risk. Delays would defer new growth avenues and prolong dependence on existing programs.
